description: I believe that every great achievement begins with a question, and every challenge is an opportunity to learn, explore and create new possibilities.
summary: This project explains how rockets help humans travel from Earth into space. It explores how rocket engines produce thrust to push rockets upwards against Earth's gravity. Rockets work using Newton's Third Law of Motion, which states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. As rockets travel higher and gain speed, they can carry astronauts, satellites and scientific equipment into space. Through this project, students can understand the science and technology behind space travel.
details: Rockets are special vehicles designed to carry astronauts, satellites and spacecraft from Earth into space. Rocket engines burn propellant and release hot gases downwards to produce thrust that pushes the rocket upwards. Rockets must produce enough thrust to overcome their weight and lift off against Earth's gravity. As the rocket gains speed, it can place spacecraft and satellites into orbit around Earth. Rocket technology allows astronauts to explore space, conduct scientific experiments and discover more about the universe.
